title: Planispheric astrolabe
summary: 25 to 65 degrees north: your plate, a lettered star rete
description: A planispheric astrolabe for a place from 25 to 65 degrees north (not the tropics, not the southern hemisphere), in brass: a mater with its degree scale, a plate of almucantars and azimuths in exact stereographic projection, a rete of lettered star pointers from the Yale Bright Star Catalogue with the ecliptic ring, a rule, and an altitude scale with an alidade on the back, to laser cut and engrave.
process: Laser or waterjet cutting of brass sheet; engraving by fibre laser or rotary cutter; letter punches for the star key; soldered limb and alidade vanes; hand finishing

difficulty.rationale: Data-driven exact projection, coupled closed-form clipping, one-face engraving and a proven, locked stack over the range.

standards: D. Abdullah, The Engineering and Programming Methods Used in Manufacture of Astrolabes and Errors Resulting, arXiv:2511.12088 (2025), eq. 5-9: closed forms of almucantars and azimuths in stereographic projection (read)
Yale Bright Star Catalogue, 5th revised edition, Hoffleit & Warren 1991 (CDS V/50), J2000.0 positions (read through the Harvard TDC ASCII file and ReadMe)
IAU Division C Working Group on Star Names, IAU-CSN (E. Mamajek), names by HR number (read; CC BY)
Mean obliquity at J2000.0, 23 deg 26 min 21.448 s (read in Wikipedia, Axial tilt; the Astronomical Almanac constant)
materials: Brass sheet CuZn37, 1 to 3 mm (8500 kg/m3)
Limb from two rings of the sheet, soft-soldered, or one ring of double thickness
Brass rod for the pin, wedge and locating pin; brass wire for the ring
Black wax or paint in the engraved lines
